transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling like I’ve really let my family down. We took on this mortgage, and it feels like that’s on me. And then at work, if I mess up even a little, it just kind of proves I’m useless… like I deserve whatever comes from it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم days?
Yeah… most days, I think. It’s like this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I just go through the motions at work, carrying plates, smiling because I’m supposed to… not because I actually feel okay.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t really joke around with the regulars like I used to. After shifts I used to text my brother, just stupid stuff, but now I mostly just… leave messages sitting there. I say what I need to say and that’s about it.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep?
I don’t know… nothing I’ve really kept track of. Sleep’s been kind of just… whatever it is, I guess.
Have you been having thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

I… I don’t have a plan to do anything to myself. But sometimes, when I’m lying there before an early shift, I think… maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Like I wouldn’t have to keep messing everything up.
Do you feel hopeless about the future?
Yeah… kind of. Most days it just feels heavy, empty. Like I’m carrying plates and putting on the smile because that’s the job, not because I actually feel much of anything good coming.
Have you been feeling this down nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Yeah… most days. It’s been like that for a while, I guess. Just this heavy, empty feeling, like I’m doing the work and smiling because I have to, not because I actually feel okay.
Did these feelings start after the mortgage situation became a problem?
Yeah… I think so. It’s been going on since after I took on the condo mortgage. About… a year and eight months, I guess.
Before the mortgage situation, had you ever gone through another period like this where you felt down most days for at least two weeks?

I… I don’t know. I’ve had low stretches before, I guess, but this heavy, empty feeling most days—just going through the motions, smiling because I’m supposed to—that’s more what it’s been like lately.
If the mortgage problem were resolved, do you think you’d still feel this down?
I don’t know… maybe. Even if it got fixed, most days I still have this heavy, empty feeling. Like I’m just carrying plates and smiling because I’m supposed to, not because I actually feel good.
Before this started after the mortgage, was there ever another time in your life when you felt this same kind of depression most days for at least two weeks?
Not really… not like this. I mean, I’ve had bad days, but this heavy, empty feeling most days—just kind of moving through work and smiling because I have to—that’s been more since then.
Have you had a big drop in your energy?
I’m not sure… maybe a little, but I haven’t really been paying attention to it. I still get through my shifts.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah… some. At work mostly. I’ll be putting numbers into the POS or doing inventory sheets, and I just… stare at the screen. I’ve done it for years, but lately I don’t trust what I just entered.
Do you worry excessively about a lot of different things, not just the mortgage?
I don’t think so… not a lot of different things. Mostly it’s just the mortgage stuff that gets in my head. Other things, I guess I worry some, but not like that.
Even on days when the mortgage isn’t on your mind, do you still feel depressed?

Yeah… I think so. Even when I’m not thinking about the mortgage, there’s still this heavy, empty feeling. I just kind of get through the day, smile at tables because I’m supposed to, but I don’t really feel… much good.
Before this current period, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed like this nearly every day for at least two weeks, and then it went away?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had low stretches before, but I don’t know if it was nearly every day for two weeks or if it just felt like a rough patch.
Before the mortgage situation, was there ever a time when you felt depressed like this nearly every day for at least two weeks and then later returned to your usual self?
I don’t really know. I’ve had times where I was down, sure, but I can’t say it was like this nearly every day for two weeks and then I just went back to normal. It’s kind of blurry.
Has this been making it harder for you to function at work or at home?

Yeah… somewhat. I’ve almost missed a couple shifts, and at work I’m making more little mistakes with the POS reports and inventory. At home, the mortgage paperwork’s been harder to keep straight.

I don’t like saying it, but I worry if I mess up too much I could lose the job, and then… the condo. I’ve also been keeping to myself more. My brother and people at work have noticed I’m not really acting like me.
Do you often feel worthless or excessively guilty?

Yeah… I guess I do. I keep feeling like I’ve let my family down with the mortgage. And when I make some small mistake at work, it feels like it proves I’m just… useless, like maybe I deserve whatever happens.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Yeah… a couple people at work have said something. Sometimes I’m pacing around, checking the same tables or receipts over and over. Other times I guess I’m just… slow, like getting menus or walking to the POS takes me longer than it should.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a current depressive episode with depressed mood, anhedonia, hopelessness, passive death wishes, guilt/worthlessness, concentration problems, psychomotor change, and functional impairment persisting most days for far longer than 2 weeks. Recurrent depressive disorder was considered but prior distinct episodes were not established.
